privacyDataBody: meYou has no account and no company server. Your profile, settings, diary and everything you add stay on this phone until you connect your own server in Settings. Diary memories are shared with your partner only after you are paired (see below). After that, data goes only to that server, the one you or someone you trust runs. It is never sent to any other server.
privacyServerTitle: What is sent to your server
privacyServerBody: The phone gallery is only backed up by hand, and only from the albums you choose. With automatic backup on (the default), your new memories, events and the files you add to the Archive are saved to your server in a folder for their date (Backup/year/month/day) with a small info file; events marked as a surprise are never included. In “Move” mode, once the server holds an identical copy, the app's own copy is removed from the phone. The exceptions are the photo of an event you share with your partner and a sharper copy of your profile photo: they are uploaded to your server (folder Shared) so that your partner can see them. Messages to your partner (status, events with their icon and note, diary memories with their title, text, category, mood and date, and your profile name, photo, birthday and the date you got together) are placed in a mailbox on your server. The mailbox keeps them for 30 days or the latest 1000 messages, whichever limit comes first, and then removes the older ones. Once you are paired, a new or edited memory and its deletion are sent to your partner; the number of its photos and videos is sent, the photos and videos themselves are not. Memories you wrote before pairing are not sent until you edit them. Unpairing stops this. Whoever runs the server can read what is stored on it.
privacySecurityBody: The server setup guide gives your server an HTTPS address with an automatic certificate. The app warns you when an address does not use HTTPS, because plain http is not encrypted: use it only on a network you trust. Each phone has its own secret token, kept in Android SecureStore on the phone. The token is sent in a request header, never inside an address.
privacyPushBody: When meYou is closed, your server wakes your phone through Google Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). The text is generic, for example “New status from your partner”: no emoji, note, event title or any other message content is sent through Google. Google can see that a notification was sent to your phone and when. You can turn off status, event, memory or period notifications in Settings > Partner & notifications; your server then sends nothing for that type.
privacyTrackingBody: The app contains no analytics, no advertising and no tracker. Diagnostics stay on this device unless you choose Share as text in Tools.
privacyMediaBody: Media added to the Archive or Diary stays on the device unless backup copies it to your server. The app never deletes anything on the server: it has no delete function, and a file that already exists is never overwritten. Diary attachments are copied without app-side editing or re-encoding, so embedded file metadata is not removed.
privacyLogsBody: Your server logs only the type of request (the route, not the full address), the result, the time, the IP address and the device id. It never logs tokens, file names or message text. After many different wrong tokens or invitation codes from one IP address, the server refuses that address for a while.
privacyRevokeBody: If a phone is lost, the person who runs the server cuts it off on the server: sudo ./setup.sh devices lists the phones, sudo ./setup.sh revoke <id> revokes one, and sudo ./setup.sh rotate-token issues a new token. The phone's token stops working at once. Removing a server inside the app only forgets it on this phone: it does not revoke the token and does not delete anything on the server.
termsUseBody: meYou is a personal app for recording status, events and diary entries, for sharing status, events and diary memories with one partner, for browsing and backing up your photos and videos to your own server, and for showing the Days together widget.
termsStorageBody: There is no account and no cloud service from the developer. Your data lives on this phone and, if you connect one, on your own server. meYou can copy photos and videos to that server, but it is not a backup guarantee: keep your own copy of the server's data (the server guide shows how). The app never deletes anything on the server.
termsServerBody: You, or the person you trust, run the server and are responsible for its security, updates, disk space and backups. Whoever has access to the server or to a phone's token can see what is stored for that household. A server holds one couple (two phones).
termsPartnerBody: Status, events, diary memories (text, category, mood, date, photo count), period updates and profile details you send to your partner are delivered through your server's mailbox, kept for 30 days or the latest 1000 messages. Notifications for a closed app use Google FCM with a generic text and no message content. Unpairing stops sharing with that partner; it does not erase what the partner already received on their phone.
termsAccessBody: A phone that was revoked on the server is refused until it gets a new link. After many wrong tokens or invitation codes the server may refuse an address for a while; wait and try again. You are responsible for keeping your tokens and links private.
termsResetBody: Reset settings restores preferences to their defaults while keeping your language and onboarding state. It does not delete your profile or saved media, status, diary entries or events.

Removing does not revoke the token; to cut a phone off, revoke it on the server. To connect again you need the link or QR code from your server, and a revoked token needs a new link.

privacyDriveBody: If you sign in with Google, meYou talks to Google Drive directly from this phone. Photos and videos you add in the Drive view, and the files of new memories, go into your own Google Drive, and the Archive and Explore read from it. With Drive connected, automatic backup also goes to Google Drive instead of the personal server. Nothing from Drive passes through the personal server, and the sign-in stays with Google Play services on the phone. meYou can move files and folders to the Drive bin when you ask it to (never a permanent delete). Signing out stops all access, and you can also remove meYou in your Google account settings.
termsDriveBody: Google Drive is your own Google account and is governed by Google's terms. meYou only reads and writes what you ask it to. Moving something to the Drive bin is your decision, and it can be restored there for 30 days. Keep your own copy of anything important: Drive storage limits, account problems and mistakes are outside meYou's control.
